args.issue: Incident retro (May 14) for session ct_sess_01J3Q0CF8R9B5Q2W3H7F6S2G6T: API latency spike—determine whether primary driver was cache stampede on popular queries vs DB connection pool saturation; must validate without downtime > 2 hours.
steps: Reconstruct timeline: correlate 5xx rate, p95/p99 latency, DB CPU, connection pool utilization, cache hit rate, and request QPS by endpoint for 30 min before/after spike.
Split traffic by endpoint: identify top N endpoints contributing to latency/5xx; compare with cache-key distribution (hot keys).
If cache hit rate drops or hot-key amplification exists: simulate stampede using replay in staging; test single-flight/locking and jittered TTL.
If DB pool saturation: inspect pool wait time, max connections, and slow query logs; run explain plans for top offenders; test pool sizing and backpressure.
Verification (no-downtime): deploy canary with mitigation flags (single-flight, rate limiting, circuit breaker) and confirm p99 latency + 5xx improvements under comparable load.
args.findings: Hypothesis-driven plan prepared; will decide between cache stampede vs pool saturation based on correlated metrics (cache hit/hot keys vs pool wait/max connections).
args.resolution: Implement least-risk mitigations first behind feature flags (request coalescing/single-flight for hot keys, jittered TTL, and DB pool backpressure); validate via canary and rollback-ready deployment to keep downtime under 2 hours.

args.context: Session ct_sess_01J3Q0CF8R9B5Q2W3H7F6S2G6T (Incident retro: API latency spike May 14). Goal: prevent recurrence by moving expensive synchronous read/compute paths off the request thread. Must be deployable with canary/feature flags and keep downtime < 2 hours.
implementation: Identify endpoints with highest contribution to p99/5xx; isolate expensive work (fan-out calls, heavy aggregation, cache-miss recomputation).
Introduce async job queue for recomputation and pre-warming of hot cache keys; serve stale-while-revalidate responses where acceptable.
Add request coalescing (single-flight) per cache key to prevent stampede on miss; add jittered TTL and negative caching for known misses.
Add backpressure: shed load or degrade gracefully when DB pool wait exceeds threshold; circuit breaker around downstream dependencies.
Verification: canary deploy with metric guards (p99 latency, 5xx rate, cache hit rate, DB pool wait); rollback on regression.
benefits: Reduces synchronous latency spikes by decoupling heavy work from request path
Limits stampede amplification and protects DB during cache misses
Enables gradual rollout with feature flags and canary verification
tradeoffs: Eventual consistency / serving stale data in some scenarios
Operational overhead for queue + worker scaling and monitoring
Requires careful idempotency and job deduplication

args.context: Apply a security design pattern to the decision session “Renewal strategy: Snowflake vs Databricks for analytics stack” (ct_sess_01J3Q0B7H1Y8W9Q6JX3G2Q4V8M) to ensure SOC 2 + HIPAA compliance during 2027–2028 analytics workloads and during migration/cutover.

Centralize IAM (SSO + SCIM), enforce least-privilege roles, and implement break-glass access with approval + logging.
Encrypt in transit (TLS) and at rest (KMS-managed keys); rotate keys; document key custody for audit.
Implement audit logging to a tamper-evident store; retain logs per policy; alert on privileged actions and data exfil signals.
Use tokenization/masking for sensitive fields in non-prod; enforce row/column-level security where applicable.
Establish compliance gates for migration: control mapping, evidence collection plan, and pre-cutover audit checklist.
benefits: Meets SOC 2/HIPAA control expectations with explicit technical and procedural measures.
Reduces migration risk by making compliance a gated requirement (not an afterthought).
Improves audit readiness with durable evidence and logging.
tradeoffs: Adds upfront implementation effort and potential platform constraints on convenience features.
May increase costs (segmented environments, logging retention, security tooling).
